newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to contribute troops to Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to contribute troops to Albania force.

text.p: The Danish government will send 65 soldiers to join an Italian-led multinational security force in Albania, Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said on Tuesday.
"The main task will be to ensure that humanitarian aid reaches its destination in an orderly way," he told reporters after the cabinet's weekly meeting.

The cabinet proposal, expected to be ratified by parliament this week, said the Danes would join the French battalion in Albania. Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said last week that the Danish force would arrive in Albania by around May 10.
A first wave of over 1,000 Italian, French and Spanish troops began arriving in Albania on Tuesday to prepare the way for the rest of the 6,000-strong, eight-nation mission.
The force has been tasked to safeguard the distribution of aid to the troubled Balkan state, which sank into near anarchy after fraudulent savings schemes collapsed early this year.
Nearly 300 people have been killed and 700 injured in violence which erupted in February. Albania requested international military help in early March.
